note: Static contract only: a plugin package directory in, one verdict per rule out. It does not mount the package (that is mount-admission and compat-live), does not reach the market, and never rewrites plugin source. Verification labels: evidence paths are the repository files a reader can check; a verdict carries the basis it was decided from.

severities.refuse: this package cannot be admitted this way

rules.what: the directory is a package: package.json exists, parses, and names a package
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/import-resolution.json (counts.not-a-package) plus the walk in scripts/check-import-resolution.mjs:24-46: a directory without a readable manifest is classified not-a-package, and the loader mounts rows by package name, so such a directory cannot be admitted

rules.what: every path declared in dsh.bundle.patch exists, and a package that declares none contributes no rows
rules.evidence: core/deepseek-harness/packages/boot/app-boot/src/config-schema/document.ts:14 (a row name is a plugin module specifier) and the composer at scripts/compose-profile-rows.mjs:107-111, which records a missing declared patch as a limit instead of mounting it

rules.what: a patch file is a top-level array of mappings; anything else is not a patch list
rules.evidence: core/deepseek-harness/vendor/include/src/index.ts:230-232 throws TypeError(config file must be a top-level array of entries) for every non-array document

rules.what: a non-insert row carries a nonempty id, an insert child carries id and name, and one file does not insert the same id twice
rules.evidence: core/deepseek-harness/packages/boot/app-boot/src/config-schema/document.ts:11-31 (the metadata key list, the insert shape, and non-insert rows replacing supplied fields); the class vocabulary this mirrors is read from compat/adaptation/rows/reports/rows.json counts.byClass (skipped-no-id, duplicate-insert-id, unknown-metadata-key)

rules.what: an id this package inserts is also claimed by a later layer of this repository composition
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/rows/profile-composition.json (each id carries mentions with layer order and the configSuperseded flag); the same fact is an item of category row-config-superseded in compat/adaptation/port-verdicts.json

rules.what: a bare module a row names resolves from the package or is a package the kernel itself provides
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/loader-boot.json case negative-missing-module (raw reading: the row is reported as failed to import and the entry does not activate) together with compat/adaptation/import-resolution.json (classes resolves, dependency-not-installed, undeclared-not-found, peer-not-installed)

rules.what: a bare specifier the package own files import is declared in dependencies, peerDependencies or optionalDependencies
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/import-resolution.json counts: undeclared-not-found 2 and dependency-not-installed 5 out of 72 rows, each row carrying the at file:line that names the specifier

rules.what: a peer range on a kernel package admits the kernel version this build carries
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/usage-targets.json records dsh-search-failover peer ^0.1.0-rc.6 against kernel 0.2.1-alpha.1; compat/adaptation/port-verdicts.json carries three items of category peer-range-excludes-kernel, severity rewrite

rules.what: a client-plane usage names a service the captured client surface declares
rules.evidence: compat/surface/client-0.2.1-alpha.1.json (39 services with declaredIn); compat/adaptation/port-verdicts.json carries client-service-absent (3) and host-callsite-absent (2), both severity rewrite; compat/adaptation/client-plane.json judges the same usage per plugin

rules.what: a client-plane usage names a member the captured member set of that service declares
rules.evidence: compat/surface/client-0.2.1-alpha.1.json services[].members/membersComplete/membersReason (28 complete, 2 partial, 9 unreadable) and compat/adaptation/client-plane.json member-present/member-unknown rows; a member is absent only when the set was enumerated completely

rules.what: the package declares a licence, and it is one the host may load
rules.evidence: compat/adaptation/third-party-scan.json hits[].license and compat/adaptation/port-verdicts.json verdicts[].license: the admission pipeline records the declared licence for every package it judges (all seven are MIT), so a package that declares none is unread rather than fine
